_comment: THE REPOSITORY ROOT's DECLARATION — what this instance IS and which directories it holds. SPLIT back out of `folio-assistant.config.json` on 2026-09-21, when the owner reversed `b5f0` §1's REPLACE ruling and took its other option: `<name>.json` for the declaration, `<name>.config.json` for the config, so the pair is legible from the filenames alone. Before the split both files ended `.config.json` and were told apart only by which directory they sat in and whether they carried a `name` — two schemas, two readers, one filename shape, which is the confusion `b5f0` §1 named when it recorded the option. Read by `readDeclaration` against `CatHarnessDeclarationSchema`; its sibling `folio-assistant.config.json` is read by `readHarnessConfig` and carries `contentType`. The root is the one instance where these were merged, because its instance directory IS the repository root — every other instance already had them in different directories.

description: The repository itself, acting as an initialized instance. NAMED `folio-assistant-checkout` rather than `folio-assistant`, which `cat-harness/harness.json` already uses: two declarations sharing a name makes `declaredBy` and a sticky's `contributedBy` ambiguous, so a directory can be attributed to the wrong instance while reading correctly. _avatar_comment: THE ROOT INSTANCE, and it had no entry until 2026-09-22 — bean `zc7m`. Owner, reporting it: *"folio assistant icon is messed up still. I want theme like in avaatars"*. It was the GENERIC question mark, which is what `avatarFor` returns for a name nothing declares, and the table's own header has carried the instruction the whole time: *"bootstrap has avatar, so does cat-harness, folio-asst"*. Two of those three were here. TONE 236, between `folio` (224) and `tools` (250), and deliberately near `folio-assistant-core`'s 212 — the same reasoning the three kinds below `cat-harness` are given: these are parts of one graph and a reader scanning a legend should see them as a family. Far enough to tell apart, close enough that neither reads as belonging somewhere else. THE GLYPH IS THE CORE'S LEAF, HELD. `folio-assistant-core` is the leaf of paper; the root instance is what holds one, so this is that leaf inside a frame rather than a second unrelated mark. An instance and its core drawn as two unrelated things would be the same drift the tones avoid. Moved here from cat-harness/schemas/avatars.ts, 2026-10-05 (bean sod4 #4): an instance declares its own mark.

directories.description: The incoming queue of the document-ingestion pipeline for THIS checkout — raw files as dropped, before ingestion. Distinct from `cat-harness/uploads/`, which is the harness layer's own queue: the two are different instances' directories that happen to share an id, not one directory declared twice. NOT L1 and NOT greppable as corpus; a source sitting here reads as absent to every consumer while the file is on disk.

The Tool-node barrel. `index.ts` merges every instance's `<stub>/tools/*.ts` into the one import five consumers use -- `check-tools`, `kg-export`, `harness-schema-export`, `tool-coverage` and the MCP projection -- so adding an instance is one line here rather than a path baked into five call sites. Declared by the ROOT rather than by `cat-harness` with repository scope: it is the checkout's own barrel over every instance, and repository-scoped entries from `cat-harness` are what put 15 paths under two declarations each.

directories._coverage_comment: THE OWNER RULED, 2026-09-21: render it, keep it off the canonical deploy. They asked to see this graph ("i eant to see beans/ todos/ fsh-guts/") and the description below says it is DELIBERATELY unrendered so something can be kept without being published. Both were wanted, so `publish: "staging-only"` is the third answer: `compose-docs.ts` withholds the page unless told `--staging`, which a local build and a STAGING preview pass and the canonical deploy does not. The default is the restrictive one because the two failure directions are not symmetric -- a forgotten flag loses a page from a preview, where whoever is looking at the preview sees it missing, while the opposite default publishes withheld content with nothing to show for it. The page INDEXES rather than republishes: each entry links to the file, so the graph stays the one copy.
directories.description: The trashcan that is kept. Deprecated and throwaway structured content — addressable, exported as <base>/fsh-guts.jsonld, and DELIBERATELY absent from the rendered site. Every other declared kind here is non-renderable because it is a graph a tool reads and there was never a page to make of it; this one's contents could be rendered and are not, so that something can be kept without being published. It is also the destination that makes the never-delete rule enforceable beyond beans: AGENTS.md forbids deleting a bean because a scrapped item stops the next agent re-entering a dead end while a deleted one cannot be told from an accident, and that reasoning was always general — an agent removing a page or a script had only `rm`. Delete now means relocate here, and relocate is reversible. Files declare themselves with `$schema: folio-fsh-guts/v1`, per the same contract the bean and workflow stores use. NOTE on the name: `.fsh` is FHIR Shorthand in this codebase and across the WHO SMART folios; the collision was raised and the owner confirmed this spelling. REPOSITORY-scoped: it sits at the top of the checkout, not inside this instance, and it is deliberately never overlaid by a dependency.

directories.description: How a PERSON wants to be asked — committed, read at session start by every agent. `context` by the same test as agent memory: read during a process, never written by one, changed when a person states a preference. It sat in `.harness/`, undeclared, until 2026-09-20, which this repository's own dot-prefix guard forbids: a dot-prefixed directory is absent from a plain `ls`, from most file browsers and from a forge's web tree, and the file read at the start of every session was in the one place the conventions reject. The path is also `harness.config.json`'s `interaction` key, which defaults here — the declaration and the config now name the same place instead of one of them being a literal nobody checks. SCOPE IS `repository`, and omitting it was a live defect for an hour on 2026-09-20: without it the path resolves against the INSTANCE, so a consumer looked in `cat-harness/` while the content sat at the repository root — and `harness:dirs` then created the empty instance-level directory to satisfy the declaration, turning declared-but-absent into declared-and-empty, which is the `dh4f` false pass wearing a tidier face. Repository, not instance, for the same reason `beans/` and `todos/` are: these are read by every agent working in this repository, not by this instance's code.

directories.description: THE REPOSITORY ROOT'S DOCUMENTATION OVERLAY, managed by this instance. Owner's ruling, 2026-09-21, answering whether the root declares its own docs: "harness can have docs/ which then get listed under cat-harness/docs/<harness>, there is also docs/ dir in repo root managed by cat-harness. other harness augment or overlay ontop of that (content and behviors)". SEPARATE FROM THE `docs` ENTRY ABOVE, AND IT HAS TO BE. That one is instance-scoped and `reproduce`, which is what makes a DEPENDENT materialise its own docs/ (bean n0nf slice 1). This one is `scope: "repository"`, and a repository-scoped entry is filtered out for dependencies -- cat-harness.ts:3261 and :3507 both skip it unless `link.own`. Re-scoping the existing entry instead of adding this one would therefore have UNDONE slice 1 silently: a dependent would simply stop getting a docs/ and nothing would fail. Two directories answering two questions, so two entries, with distinct ids -- the convention `who-iris-docs` already follows. `dependents` is `skip` for the same reason every other cross-instance repository-scoped entry here is: a dependent never reaches this one at all, and claiming it reproduces would be a promise the resolver does not keep. WHAT MAKES IT NOT `dh4f`: a declared directory that nothing reads is this repository's most-paid-for defect, and an empty overlay is exactly that shape. It is consumed by the site build, which composes it OVER cat-harness/docs/ -- so what it contributes today is nothing VERIFIABLY, pinned by a test asserting an empty overlay produces a byte-identical site, rather than nothing unnoticed.

_assets_comment: THE REPOSITORY'S OWN TWO FILES, declared here as of 2026-09-20 (issue #592). Before that the root instance declared NO assets at all, and `cat-harness` declared both of these with `scope: "repository"` — so the file an agent reads first was simultaneously "what this repository is" and "what the cat-harness layer is", and no instance owned it. `check:subgraph-coverage` reported nothing, because the asset DID resolve; it resolved to the wrong file's job, which is a distinction that check could not make until this split gave it two files to tell apart. The owner settled the fork on 2026-09-20: split them, so every instance owns exactly one README and one AGENTS.md, the root's being the INDEX over the others.

assets.title: AGENTS.md — folio-assistant
assets.description: The file every cold agent reads first, and the rules that bind in EVERY layer of this checkout. A layer's own AGENTS.md augments it and never restates it. `source` names the bootstrap instance it descends from, so "is this still what it was copied from" is a question that can be ASKED — 'it was copied at init' is not an answer. This provenance sits here rather than on cat-harness's because THIS is the file bootstrap copies at initialisation; cat-harness's own is authored in place and carries no source.

assets.title: folio-assistant
assets.description: The repository's reader-facing entry point, and the INDEX over every instance in it: its `cat-harness:instances` section is generated from the declarations themselves, giving each instance both an agent entry (AGENTS.md, memories) and a human one (README, docs). Generated sections are written by `readme:sync` only where the file already carries their markers, and `readme:audit` verifies every other link.

_needs_comment: THE CHECKOUT AGGREGATES (bean cmsl option A, owner 2026-09-30 round 3; placement PR0, bean ejye): the root instance `needs` EVERY instance this checkout stages, so a corpus-wide tool resolves a kind over this instance's overlay (`checkoutDirectories` in schemas/harness-config.ts) instead of asking the platform, which until PR0 named 19 of its own dependents' directories with `scope: "repository"`. The arrow is now the right way round: the checkout depends on what it contains, nobody depends on the checkout, and the platform names no folio. Before PR0 this was `["folio-assistant-core"]` and the layering was the owner's 2026-09-20 sentence, "So bootsteap, cat harness, fa-core, f-a, from bottom to top" — which still holds: every instance listed here sits on that stack through its own `needs`. `check:instance-graph` refuses an instance in this checkout that this list omits.

stickies._comment: THE ROOT INSTANCE'S OWN CARD. Owner, 2026-09-23: "engineer for root". A theme is reached THROUGH a sticky -- an instance contributes a card, the card names a theme, the theme names an imageRole, and the images carrying that role supply the art. So this exists for the navbar mark, and it also puts the root on the landing board; that is inherent to the mechanism rather than a side effect nobody chose. THE ART IS CAT-HARNESS'S, not this instance's: the root declares no images, and `landing-engineer` is declared one level down. That is the supplier-is-not-the-subject case `bootstrap` already relies on, and the reason theme art resolves against the site owner's image set as a fallback. ORDER 5, ahead of cat-harness's 10: this instance IS the repository, so it reads first. `STICKY_ORDER_LEADING` is 10 and `STICKY_ORDER_TRAILING` 90, so 5 sits outside the leading slot deliberately rather than tying with it -- an absent order is a tie with everything, and so is a duplicated one.
